raw_segments.text: Brutus. Cassius, be not deceived. If I have veiled my look I turn the trouble of my countenance
merely upon myself. Vexed I am of late with passions of some difference, conceptions only
proper to myself, which give some soil perhaps to my behaviors. But let not therefore my
good friends be grieved, among which number, Cassius, be you one, nor construe any further
my neglect, than that poor Brutus with himself at war forgets the shows of love to other
